rows.source: HSE ionising-radiation workplace protection
rows.verified: The Ionising Radiations Regulations 2017 apply across workplaces using radioactive substances, radiation-emitting equipment and relevant natural radiation sources.

rows.source: HSE ionising-radiation workplace protection
rows.verified: Employers must keep exposure to ionising radiation as low as reasonably practicable and below statutory dose limits.

rows.source: HSE ionising-radiation workplace protection
rows.verified: Exposure restriction should prioritise engineering controls and design, followed by safe systems of work, with personal protective equipment as a last resort.

rows.source: HSE ionising-radiation workplace protection
rows.verified: Before relevant work, employers must complete a radiation risk assessment covering normal exposure and reasonably foreseeable radiation accidents.

rows.source: HSE ionising-radiation workplace protection
rows.verified: Employers must prepare contingency plans for foreseeable radiation accidents and rehearse them at suitable intervals where appropriate.

rows.source: HSE ionising-radiation workplace protection
rows.verified: Radiation employers must consult a suitable radiation protection adviser on specified compliance matters.

rows.source: HSE ionising-radiation workplace protection
rows.verified: Radiation risk assessment should estimate likely doses, determine monitoring needs and identify whether workers require classified-person status.

rows.source: HSE ionising-radiation workplace protection
rows.verified: Workers likely to exceed specified annual dose thresholds must be designated as classified persons, medically supervised and have doses assessed and recorded.

rows.source: HSE ionising-radiation workplace protection
rows.verified: Ionising-radiation risk depends on source type and activity, shielding, distance, exposure time, work method, containment, monitoring, competence and accident potential.

rows.source: HSE ionising-radiation workplace protection
rows.verified: HSE radiation evidence is source-, task-, worker-, dose-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level health probability.

rows.source: HSE bakery flour-dust and asthma control
rows.verified: Flour dust can cause eye and nose irritation, occupational dermatitis and occupational asthma.

rows.source: HSE bakery flour-dust and asthma control
rows.verified: Flour dust is a hazardous substance under COSHH and exposure should be reduced as far below the workplace exposure limit as reasonably practicable.

rows.source: HSE bakery flour-dust and asthma control
rows.verified: Bakery additives containing enzymes such as fungal alpha-amylase are potent sensitisers and their airborne exposure should be minimised.

rows.source: HSE bakery flour-dust and asthma control
rows.verified: HSE COSHH guidance covers bag opening, tipping, dough mixing and other bakery tasks using dust extraction and equivalent effective controls.

rows.source: HSE bakery flour-dust and asthma control
rows.verified: Bakers should avoid raising dust clouds and use extraction or suitable respiratory protection for dusty tasks.

rows.source: HSE bakery flour-dust and asthma control
rows.verified: Dry sweeping and compressed-air cleaning should be avoided; wet cleaning or an industrial vacuum should be used instead.

rows.source: HSE bakery flour-dust and asthma control
rows.verified: Mixers should start slowly until wet and dry ingredients combine, and controlled dredgers or sprinklers can reduce dust during flour application.

rows.source: HSE bakery flour-dust and asthma control
rows.verified: HSE testing indicates low-dust flour can reduce airborne dust where flour must be used as a release agent.

rows.source: HSE bakery flour-dust and asthma control
rows.verified: Bakery respiratory risk depends on flour and additive type, dustiness, task, handling speed, extraction, cleaning, exposure duration and worker sensitisation.

rows.source: HSE bakery flour-dust and asthma control
rows.verified: HSE bakery evidence is ingredient-, task-, workplace-, control-, worker- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level asthma probability.
